name: Surrey Hills
title: Garden Supplies Surrey Hills | Delivered Under 2 Hrs | SHGS
metaDescription: Mulch, soil, sand and rock from our Surrey Hills yard on Canterbury Road. Bulk delivery by the cubic metre in under 2 hours, or bags and BYO trailer.
h1: Garden Supplies Delivered to Surrey Hills
intro: The yard is on Canterbury Road, so if you live in Surrey Hills you are our closest customer. Pick up bags, bring a trailer, or have a bulk load tipped in your driveway by the cubic metre. Most Surrey Hills deliveries are on the truck and gone within the hour.
body: Surrey Hills is where we are, and it is the suburb we know best. The streets between Canterbury Road and Riversdale Road are a mix of Federation and interwar brick homes on generous blocks, a lot of them with deep back gardens that have been planted and replanted over the better part of a century. Mature elms, liquidambars and plane trees line many of the streets, so there is plenty of shade, plenty of leaf drop, and the usual heavy clay underneath once you dig past the topsoil.

That combination shapes what locals order. Established beds under big trees get topped up with 10mm pine bark because fallen leaves blend into it and it does not blow around in a northerly. Tired beds that have been worked for decades get a few cubic metres of organic mulch forked through to put some life back into the clay. When someone pulls out an old lawn or builds a raised bed, blended soil is the usual call, and for a new path or shed base we load crushed rock and washed sand onto the same truck.
Ordering from a yard that is already in the suburb

Being local changes how people buy. A lot of Surrey Hills customers simply drive down Canterbury Road with the trailer on, get loaded, and are back home spreading mulch twenty minutes later. Others grab a few 15kg bags on the way past for a planter box or a patch of lawn repair. For anything over a trailer load it makes more sense to have us deliver it in bulk by the cubic metre; the truck tips it where you want it, on the nature strip or in the driveway, and you are not shovelling it out of a trailer twice.

Because the run from the yard to anywhere in Surrey Hills is only a few minutes, we can usually fit a local delivery in around the longer runs out to the east. Tell us roughly where on the block you want the load tipped, keep the spot clear of cars, and put a tarp down if you are ordering coloured mulch near pavers.

Not sure how many metres you need? Measure the bed, tell us the depth you are after, and we will do the sums for you. Call the yard on (03) 9890 3901, or come in and have a look at the bays before you decide.

faqs.q: How quickly can you deliver within Surrey Hills?
faqs.a: Surrey Hills is the yard's own suburb, so a bulk load is usually on its way well inside our under-2-hour promise. Call ahead and we will tell you where you sit in the day's run.

faqs.q: Should I bring my trailer or order a bulk delivery?
faqs.a: For a single trailer load it is often quicker to drive down Canterbury Road and get loaded. For anything bigger, or if you do not want to shovel it twice, a bulk delivery by the cubic metre is the easier option.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum order for Surrey Hills deliveries?
faqs.a: Call for current minimums and delivery fees. Smaller amounts can be picked up in 15kg bags from the yard at any time.

intro: Box Hill is a short run east along Canterbury Road from our yard, about five to ten minutes depending on the lights at Elgar Road. We deliver bulk loads by the cubic metre to Box Hill, Box Hill North and Box Hill South, and plenty of Box Hill customers pick up bags or bring a trailer.
body: Few suburbs in Melbourne's east have changed as much as Box Hill over the last fifteen years. The streets around Box Hill Central are now apartment towers, while the blocks further out in Box Hill North and Box Hill South are being split, with a 1950s brick veneer coming down and two or three townhouses going up in its place. Each of those townhouses has a small courtyard, a strip of side garden and a front setback that needs finishing, and that is the kind of job we supply every week.

Small outdoor spaces push people towards low-maintenance finishes. Synthetic lawn is popular in Box Hill courtyards, which means a compacted base of crusher dust, a roll of Smart Grass and a few bags of kiln dried sand to dress the pile. For the planted strips along the fence, black midnight mulch suits the dark render and timber cladding most of these builds use. Where a builder has left nothing but subsoil behind, a metre or two of blended soil gets a garden started.

The older part of Box Hill is a different job. Interwar homes near Box Hill Gardens still sit on full-size blocks with lawn out the front and a vegie patch and fruit trees behind, and those gardens take the same mix of mulch, soil and sand that the rest of the east does. The clay is heavy here too, so gypsum from the garden products shelf often goes on the truck with the soil.
Getting it to a tight site

Access is the thing to think about in Box Hill. New townhouse developments often share a narrow driveway, and apartment buildings have nowhere to tip a bulk load at all. If that is your situation, 15kg bags from the yard are the practical answer, and a ute or trailer can be loaded at the yard with whatever you need. Where there is a driveway or a clear nature strip, bulk delivery by the cubic metre is cheaper per metre and saves you the trip.

Tell us the address and where you want the load tipped when you ring, and mention if the street has parking restrictions or a body corporate that needs notice. Call (03) 9890 3901 to organise a Box Hill delivery or to check what is in the bays today.

faqs.q: How long does delivery to Box Hill take?
faqs.a: Box Hill is one of the closest suburbs to the yard, about five to ten minutes along Canterbury Road. We deliver in less than two hours across Melbourne's east, and Box Hill runs are usually well inside that.

faqs.q: I live in a townhouse with a shared driveway. Can you still deliver?
faqs.a: Usually, as long as there is a spot the truck can tip onto without blocking neighbours. If there is not, we can load your trailer or ute at the yard, or you can take 15kg bags.

faqs.q: What is the minimum bulk order for Box Hill?
faqs.a: Call for current minimums and delivery fees. Anything under a trailer load is generally easier to collect in bags.

The gardens match the houses: formal front lawns, clipped hedges, rose beds, and a lot of old brick paths, edging and retaining walls that need patching from time to time. Many of these properties have been in the same hands for decades and the owners know exactly what they want.

The product list reflects that. 10mm pine bark is the mulch of choice for beds near the house because it sits flat and looks tidy against a heritage facade, while the bigger beds under old oaks and elms take 20mm pine bark that spreads further and needs topping up less often. Vegie gardens and new plantings go into premium organic soil. For the gravel paths and driveways that suit these houses, Tuscan toppings give a warm, period-appropriate finish, and we keep white brick sand for anyone repointing a garden wall or relaying a brick path.
Delivery to Canterbury

With the yard this close, delivery is simple. Bulk loads go out by the cubic metre and are tipped on the driveway or nature strip, and because it is such a short run we can often slot a Canterbury drop between bigger deliveries further out. If you only need a bit, 15kg bags from the yard are quick to collect, and a BYO trailer gets loaded on the spot. The streets around Canterbury are wide, so truck access is rarely an issue, but let us know if there is a low overhanging tree or a tight crossover.

One thing to keep in mind: the soil around here is Melbourne's usual heavy clay once you are past the topsoil, and some of the older beds have become hydrophobic after years of mulching with fine material. Forking through organic mulch or adding washed sand to the soil before planting helps with both problems. Ask when you ring and we will suggest the right mix.
Ring the yard on (03) 9890 3901 with your address and the number of metres, or drop in on Canterbury Road to see the products before you order.

Camberwell keeps a lot of landscapers and builders busy, and we supply both the trade and the owner doing it themselves. There is a steady interest in native planting here too, so native garden mix for grevilleas and kangaroo paws is a regular order, and for the brick paths and small paving jobs that come with these houses we supply washed sand and crushed rock for the base.

name: Blackburn
title: Garden Supplies Blackburn | Delivered Under 2 Hrs | SHGS
metaDescription: Native mix, pine bark, scoria and drainage supplies delivered to Blackburn in under 2 hours from the Surrey Hills yard. Bulk by the cubic metre or trailer.
intro: Blackburn is about ten to twelve minutes east of the yard along Canterbury Road. We deliver bulk mulch, soil, sand and stone to Blackburn, Blackburn North and Blackburn South by the cubic metre, and the drive is short enough for a trailer run.
body: Blackburn is the greenest suburb we deliver to. The streets around Blackburn Lake Sanctuary and the Creeklands are under a canopy of eucalypts, and the council's tree protection rules mean that canopy is not going anywhere. Blocks here tend to be large and often sloping, with houses from the 1950s to the 1970s set back among the trees and gardens that lean towards natives and bush-style planting rather than formal lawns and hedges.

That changes what people order. Native garden mix is far more popular in Blackburn than almost anywhere else we deliver, because it drains freely and keeps the nutrient levels low the way grevilleas, banksias and correas like. Under the gums, 20mm pine bark is the mulch of choice since bark and leaf litter disappear into it. Where a bed has become tired, organic mulch forked through the clay puts organic matter back without overdoing the nutrients.

Sloping ground and clay also mean water problems. Plenty of Blackburn houses get a wet side yard or a damp slab in winter, and the fix is usually an ag drain down the high side. We supply the scoria to backfill the trench and the ag pipe, pits and geotextile from drainage supplies to go with it. A metre of scoria goes a long way in a 300mm trench, so tell us the trench length and we will work out the volume.
Getting the load in among the trees

Delivery to Blackburn is straightforward on most streets, but the tree canopy can be low over a driveway. When you ring, tell us if there are overhanging branches or a narrow crossover and the driver will tip on the nature strip instead. Bulk loads go out by the cubic metre; smaller jobs are covered by 15kg bags, and if you have a trailer or ute we will load it at the yard.
Call (03) 9890 3901 to organise a Blackburn delivery or to check what native mix and bark we have in the bays today.

faqs.a: Blackburn is about ten to twelve minutes from the yard. We deliver across Melbourne's east in less than two hours, and a Blackburn load is normally well inside that.

faqs.q: My driveway has low branches. Can the truck still get in?
faqs.a: Tell us when you order. If the driveway is not clear the driver will tip on the nature strip or another spot you nominate. Alternatively bring a trailer to the yard and we will load it.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum for scoria or native mix delivered to Blackburn?

Hard landscaping leads the orders here. Crushed rock goes under driveways and paths, and crusher dust is the compacted base for the Smart Grass that suits the small, terraced lawns these houses end up with. Our bulk concrete mix covers the fence posts, steps and small slabs that a sloping block generates, with cement, reo and bar chairs in the shop. Once the planting goes in, black midnight mulch is the finish most Doncaster builds ask for against dark render and timber battens.
Delivering on a slope

Bulk loads go out by the cubic metre and are tipped where the site has room. On a steep Doncaster driveway that needs a bit of care: loose material will roll, so the driver may suggest tipping at the top of the drive or on a flat part of the nature strip. Coloured mulch should go on a tarp if it is landing on exposed aggregate or pavers. If the site cannot take a truck, we can load a trailer or ute at the yard, or you can take as many 15kg bags as the job needs.

The ground in Doncaster is heavy clay with a lot of fill on the cut-and-fill blocks, and it drains badly on the low side of a slope. Scoria and ag pipe for a drain behind a retaining wall are worth adding to the order if the wall is going in at the same time.
Call (03) 9890 3901 with the Doncaster address and what stage the job is at, and we will line up the delivery to suit the trades on site.

faqs.q: How long does delivery to Doncaster take?
faqs.a: Doncaster is about fifteen minutes from the Surrey Hills yard. We deliver across Melbourne's east in less than two hours and Doncaster runs are usually well within that.

faqs.q: My driveway is steep. Where will the load be tipped?
faqs.a: The driver will pick the safest flat spot, usually the top of the driveway or the nature strip. Mention the slope when you order so we can plan the tip.

faqs.q: What is the minimum for a bulk delivery to Doncaster?
faqs.a: Call for current minimums and delivery fees. Smaller jobs can be collected in 15kg bags or on a trailer from the yard.

title: Garden Supplies Glen Iris | Delivered Under 2 Hrs | SHGS

h1: Garden Supplies Delivered to Glen Iris
intro: Glen Iris is about fifteen minutes south-west of the yard, down through Camberwell along Burke Road or Warrigal Road. We deliver bulk mulch, soil, sand and stone to Glen Iris by the cubic metre, and the yard is an easy trip for bags or a trailer load.
body: Glen Iris runs along Gardiners Creek, and the creek is the thing to understand about its gardens. The land slopes down to the creek from both sides, the soil is heavy clay with patches of fill, and the low streets near Ferndale Park and the Gardiners Creek Trail can get waterlogged after a big rain. The houses are mostly interwar brick and weatherboard on decent blocks, with a growing number of renovated and rebuilt homes along the High Street end.

Drainage comes up in nearly every Glen Iris conversation. An ag drain down the side of the house or behind a retaining wall needs scoria to backfill the trench and the pipe, pits and geotextile from our drainage supplies. Where the problem is the clay itself, organic mulch forked through the beds opens it up over time, and raised beds built above the clay get filled with premium organic soil. For a soakage pit or a concrete pour, 14mm screenings go on the same load.
Family gardens

Glen Iris is a family suburb and the backyards show it: a lawn for the kids, a vegie patch, a trampoline, and a sandpit, which is why triple washed sand is a regular small order here. Lawns get patched with blended soil and seed in autumn, and beds are mulched with pine bark in spring. These are mostly trailer-sized jobs, and a lot of Glen Iris customers do exactly that, driving up to the yard on a Saturday morning and getting loaded.

For a bigger job, bulk delivery by the cubic metre is tipped on the driveway or nature strip. The streets are mostly wide with good access, but the blocks that back onto the creek can have steep driveways, so mention that when you order. 15kg bags cover anything smaller and can be collected any time.
Ring the yard on (03) 9890 3901 with the Glen Iris address, the number of metres and what the job is, and we will get it sorted.

faqs.q: How long does delivery to Glen Iris take?
faqs.a: Glen Iris is about fifteen minutes from the yard. We deliver across Melbourne's east in less than two hours, and Glen Iris loads are usually well within that.

faqs.q: How much scoria do I need for a drain in Glen Iris?
faqs.a: Tell us the trench length, width and depth and we will work out the cubic metres. A typical 300mm-wide trench uses far less than people expect.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum delivery to Glen Iris?
faqs.a: Call for current minimums and delivery fees. Sandpit sand and small top-ups are easiest in 15kg bags from the yard.

name: Ashburton
title: Garden Supplies Ashburton | Delivered Under 2 Hrs | SHGS
metaDescription: Blended soil, turf, pine bark, crusher dust and cement delivered to Ashburton in under 2 hours from the Surrey Hills yard. Bulk, bags or BYO trailer.
intro: Ashburton is about fifteen minutes south of the yard down Warrigal Road. We deliver bulk soil, mulch, sand and stone to Ashburton by the cubic metre, and Ashburton customers with a ute or trailer are regulars at the Surrey Hills yard.
body: Ashburton was largely built in the 1940s and 1950s, with weatherboard and brick veneer homes on flat, regular blocks either side of High Street. Lots of those homes have been extended or knocked down and rebuilt in the last decade, and the ones that have not are often being renovated by young families who have moved in for the schools and the shops. Either way there is a lot of garden work going on, from new lawns and fences to full landscapes behind a new build.

Lawns are a big part of it. Ashburton backyards are flat and open, so instant turf over 100mm of blended soil is a job we supply constantly, with lawn seed from the shop for patching. Beds around the lawn are mulched with 10mm pine bark, which suits the tidy, low-key style of the suburb. Renovation work brings in crusher dust for paving and shed bases and cement and sand for fence posts, mortar and small slabs.
Pickup or delivery?

With the yard a quarter of an hour away, Ashburton customers split fairly evenly between collecting and having it delivered. A trailer load of soil or bark is a quick trip up Warrigal Road and we load it for you. For a new lawn, though, the soil alone is usually several cubic metres, and a bulk delivery tipped on the driveway is far less work than three trailer trips. Bags are the answer for anything small, and they are easy to grab on the way home.

The soil under Ashburton is the same clay as the rest of the east, and because the blocks are flat it does not drain especially well. Before laying turf, loosen the clay, add gypsum, and spread the blended soil over the top rather than digging it straight in. If you are building raised beds for vegies, premium organic soil is the better fill.
Call (03) 9890 3901 with the Ashburton address and what you are doing, and we will tell you how many metres you need and when the truck can be there.

faqs.q: Can I get turf and the soil for a new lawn delivered together?
faqs.a: Yes. The blended soil should go down and be levelled first, then the instant turf, which is ordered in fresh. Ring ahead and we will time both deliveries.

faqs.q: What is the minimum order for Ashburton?
faqs.a: Call for current minimums and delivery fees. Anything under a trailer load is easiest to collect in 15kg bags.

body: Nunawading is half residential and half working suburb. South of the railway line the streets are 1960s brick veneers on good-sized blocks, many of them now split into two or three units, while along Whitehorse Road and around the industrial pockets there are workshops, showrooms and small factories with yards and car parks of their own. We supply both sides: the family in a unit tidying a courtyard and the business owner who needs a car park base or a drainage trench backfilled.

On the trade side, crushed rock is the big mover, used under hardstands, driveways and slabs, with washed sand and bulk concrete mix for the concrete that follows. Reo, mesh, bar chairs and builders plastic are in the shop. On the residential side, unit developments finish their front setbacks with 20mm pine bark because it covers a lot of ground per metre, and blended soil goes in wherever the builder has left bare subsoil behind.
Delivering to units and businesses

Unit developments in Nunawading usually share a central driveway, and the question is always where the load can be tipped without blocking the neighbours. A front nature strip is the usual answer; if there is not one, a loaded trailer from the yard or 15kg bags are the fallback. Businesses are simpler: tell us the gate, the hours someone is on site and where the material goes, and the truck will tip it there. Bulk loads are sold by the cubic metre, and bigger orders can be split across the day.

The ground through Nunawading is the same heavy clay found across the east, and on the flat blocks it holds water. If you are putting down a slab or a shed base, compacting crusher dust or crushed rock over the clay first will save trouble later. For garden beds, work organic matter in before adding soil on top.
Ring the yard on (03) 9890 3901 with the Nunawading address, the quantity and whether it is a home or a business, and we will organise the delivery.

name: Ringwood

metaDescription: Pine bark, native mix, crushed rock and toppings delivered to Ringwood in under 2 hours from the Surrey Hills yard. Bulk by the cubic metre or trailer.
intro: Ringwood is the furthest east we go on this list, about twenty to twenty-five minutes from the yard along Canterbury Road and Whitehorse Road or the Eastern Freeway. It is still comfortably inside our under-2-hour delivery promise, and we deliver bulk loads to Ringwood, Ringwood East and Ringwood North by the cubic metre.
body: Ringwood is where the suburbs start to open out. Blocks are bigger than closer in, the ground rises and falls toward the Dandenongs, and the streets around Ringwood Lake Park and out toward Ringwood North are full of tall gums and native understorey. The houses are mostly brick from the 1960s onward, with a growing cluster of apartments and townhouses near Eastland and the station, but the typical Ringwood garden is still a large, treed block with lawn, sheds, a long driveway and plenty of edges to maintain.

Large blocks mean large volumes. 20mm pine bark is the mulch most Ringwood customers order because it spreads further per cubic metre and blends with the gum litter that falls on everything. Native planting is the norm this far east, so native garden mix is a steady order for new beds. Long gravel driveways and paths are common, and crushed rock for the base with Tuscan toppings on top is the usual combination. For retaining walls on the sloping blocks, large rubble rock can be ordered in for bigger jobs.
Why order from Surrey Hills?

Ringwood has local suppliers, so people sometimes ask why they would ring a yard twenty-odd minutes away. The honest answer is product and timing: if we have what you want in the bay and the truck can be there in under two hours, the distance does not matter much. Bulk loads are delivered by the cubic metre and tipped on the driveway or nature strip, and because the run is longer we try to group Ringwood deliveries so the truck arrives when you need it rather than whenever it is passing.

If you are coming to the yard, a trailer load is a reasonable trip down Canterbury Road, and 15kg bags are there for small jobs. For anything over a trailer load, though, the delivery is worth it. Ringwood's clay is heavier and stonier than closer to town, so loosening it and adding organic matter before planting is worth the effort.
Call (03) 9890 3901 with the Ringwood address, the products and the metres, and we will tell you when the truck can be there.

faqs.q: Is Ringwood within your under-2-hour delivery zone?
faqs.a: Ringwood is about twenty to twenty-five minutes from the yard and we deliver bulk loads there. The under-2-hour promise applies across Melbourne's east; ring and we will give you a realistic arrival time for the day.

faqs.q: Should I drive to Surrey Hills with a trailer or get a Ringwood delivery?
faqs.a: For one trailer load the trip is reasonable. For anything larger, a bulk delivery by the cubic metre is less work and saves repeat trips. Call for current minimums and delivery fees.

faqs.q: Can you supply large rock for a retaining wall in Ringwood?
faqs.a: Yes. Large rubble rock is ordered in on request with a minimum of 6 cubic metres and delivered in bulk. Ring to discuss the size you need.
